method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied (with further seats for the employer and the insurer, on whom the text puts real duties), with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18: a seat-neutral core (wca-core.l4, with 9 regulative rules for the duties and deadlines of the worker, the employer and the insurer) and three seat layers that restate no rule; no REFUSE (a case outside the encoding answers `not covered`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Workers Compensation Act 1951 (A1951-2), Republication No 88 (R88), effective 26 November 2025 (last amendment A2025-30), current on the ACT Legislation Register on 2026-10-20, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/A1951-2.txt (converted from the register's unauthorised DOCX). The Workers Compensation Regulation 2002 and the indexation notices are not deposited: the indexed amounts, AWE and the statutory floor are inputs.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run wca-core.l4 ; l4 run wca-seat.l4 ; l4 run wca-seat-employer.l4 ; l4 run wca-seat-insurer.l4 ; l4 run wca-cases-worker.l4 ; l4 run wca-cases-employer.l4 ; l4 run wca-cases-insurer.l4
checks.result: 209 assertions satisfied (worker 147/147, employer 29/29, insurer 33/33), 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-10-24); 15 #TRACEs with an expect line (9 breaches, 6 obligations or permissions still open), each read and as expected
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: Compensation for an injured private-sector worker in the ACT. In: s 20 (cpi indexing, the no-negative-adjustment rule) and s 77(7) (wpi indexing); ss 21-26 as inputs; pt 4.3 weekly compensation: s 36G, s 37, s 38, ss 39-42 (first 26 weeks; s 41 floor comparisons; s 42 relevant percentages and statutory ceiling), ss 43-43B, ss 44-45, s 83 as a fact; pt 4.4 permanent injuries: ss 48-51, 53-57, 59, 61 and all 54 items of Schedule 1; pt 4.6 s 77 death benefits with the dictionary's dependant, child and full-time student, and s 78; notice: s 93, s 94(2)-(3), s 95; claims: s 116(2), s 118(2), s 119, s 120(1)-(2), s 121, s 122, s 126(1), s 127, ss 128-132, s 134. Out, each answering `not covered` where a question reaches it: who is a worker (ch 3, a fact); pt 4.2A; pt 4.5 costs; hearing loss (ss 63-66), ss 58, 62, 68; vocational rehabilitation and injury management; insurance licensing, the DI fund and terrorism (ch 8); common law damages (ch 9); registered agreements, commutation and settlement (pt 4.7, s 137), s 135; imminently fatal asbestos-related disease claims (ss 116(2)(a), 121(2)(a), 122(1)(a), 128A); ss 82, 84 as facts; Comcare for ACT public servants. Read with subjects/au/social-security-act-1991/ (s 23 pension age; pt 3.14 compensation preclusion), subjects/au/fair-work-act-2009/ (national minimum wage as the statutory floor; s 130 leave, displaced by s 46), subjects/au/income-tax-assessment-act-1997/ (weekly compensation assessable), subjects/au/a-new-tax-system-family-assistance-act-1999/ (s 77(3)) and subjects/au/act/motor-accident-injuries-act-2019/ (s 98); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the injured worker (and, on the worker's death, the dependants or personal representative)
the insurer (licensed insurer, or the employer as licensed self-insurer)
